test.name: Cell Cycle and Cell Division - Test 1

qns_content.text: Which phase of the cell cycle is responsible for DNA replication?

text_solutions: The S phase (Synthesis phase) is the stage where DNA replication occurs, doubling the genetic material.

qns_content.text: What distinguishes anaphase I of meiosis from anaphase of mitosis?

options.text: Sister chromatids separate in meiosis but not in mitosis
Homologous chromosomes separate in meiosis but not in mitosis

text_solutions: In anaphase I of meiosis, homologous chromosomes separate, whereas in mitosis, sister chromatids separate.

qns_content.text: Which of the following events occurs during anaphase I of meiosis?

text_solutions: In anaphase I of meiosis, homologous chromosomes separate, reducing the chromosome number by half.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about anaphase is correct?

options.text: Sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles

text_solutions: During anaphase, sister chromatids separate and move toward opposite poles of the cell.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about cytokinesis is correct?

options.text: Plant cells divide by forming a cleavage furrow

text_solutions: In animal cells, cytokinesis occurs by forming a cleavage furrow, while in plant cells, a cell plate forms instead.

qns_content.text: Which of the following events occurs in anaphase?

options.text: Chromosomes align at the center of the cell
Sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles

text_solutions: During anaphase, sister chromatids separate and move toward opposite poles of the cell.

qns_content.text: Which phase of mitosis directly follows metaphase?

text_solutions: Anaphase follows metaphase, during which sister chromatids separate and move toward opposite poles.

qns_content.text: Which checkpoint ensures proper chromosome alignment before anaphase begins?

text_solutions: The M checkpoint ensures that all chromosomes are properly aligned at the metaphase plate before anaphase begins.

qns_content.text: What is the outcome of meiosis II?

text_solutions: Meiosis II results in four haploid daughter cells, each with half the chromosome number of the parent cell.

qns_content.text: Which of the following happens during pachytene of meiosis I?

text_solutions: During pachytene, homologous chromosomes exchange genetic material through crossing over.

qns_content.text: Which structure is responsible for chromosome movement during cell division?

text_solutions: Spindle fibers, composed of microtubules, attach to kinetochores on chromosomes and facilitate their movement.

qns_content.text: Which phase of interphase is characterized by intense metabolic activity and cell growth?

text_solutions: The G1 phase is the period between mitosis and DNA replication, characterized by active metabolism and cell growth.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about mitosis is correct?

options.text: It results in genetically identical daughter cells
It reduces the chromosome number by half

text_solutions: Mitosis produces two genetically identical daughter cells, maintaining the chromosome number of the parent cell.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about G0 phase is correct?

options.text: Cells in G0 phase cannot divide again
Cells in G0 phase are metabolically inactive
Cells in G0 phase can re-enter the cell cycle under specific conditions
G0 phase is a part of mitosis

text_solutions: Cells in G0 phase are metabolically active and can re-enter the cell cycle when needed.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the G1 phase is incorrect?

options.text: It is the first phase of interphase
Cell growth and metabolism occur in this phase

text_solutions: DNA replication does not occur in G1; it takes place in the S phase.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about telophase is correct?

text_solutions: During telophase, the nuclear membrane reforms around each set of chromosomes, which decondense.

qns_content.text: Which of the following phases is also known as the “resting phase” of the cell cycle?

text_solutions: The G0 phase is a quiescent phase where cells temporarily or permanently exit the cell cycle.

qns_content.text: Which structure helps separate chromosomes during mitosis?

text_solutions: Spindle fibers attach to chromosomes via kinetochores and help pull them apart during mitosis.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the cell cycle is correct?

options.text: Interphase consists of G1, S, and G2 phases
Mitosis is the longest phase of the cell cycle
DNA replication occurs in the G2 phase
Cell division does not occur in prokaryotes

text_solutions: Interphase consists of G1, S, and G2 phases, where the cell prepares for division. Mitosis is not the longest phase, and DNA replication occurs in the S phase.

qns_content.text: Which phase of the cell cycle is known as the "resting phase"?

text_solutions: The G0 phase is a quiescent stage where cells do not divide but remain metabolically active.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the quiescent phase (G0) is correct?

options.text: Cells in G0 never re-enter the cell cycle
G0 phase is a metabolically inactive state
Cells can re-enter the cell cycle when required
G0 phase is the shortest phase in the cell cycle

text_solutions: Cells in G0 remain metabolically active and can re-enter the cell cycle when stimulated by external signals.

qns_content.text: Which of the following occurs during telophase I of meiosis?

text_solutions: During telophase I, homologous chromosomes reach opposite poles, and nuclear membranes may reappear.

qns_content.text: What is the function of the centrioles during mitosis?

text_solutions: Centrioles help in forming spindle fibers that assist in the movement of chromosomes during mitosis.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about diplotene is correct?

text_solutions: During diplotene, chiasmata (points of crossing over) become visible as homologous chromosomes start separating.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about meiosis II is correct?

options.text: Meiosis II involves separation of homologous chromosomes

text_solutions: Meiosis II is similar to mitosis in that sister chromatids separate, but it does not reduce the chromosome number further.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is incorrect about cytokinesis?

options.text: Animal cells undergo cytokinesis by forming a cell plate
Cytokinesis differs between plant and animal cells

text_solutions: Animal cells divide by forming a cleavage furrow, whereas plant cells form a cell plate.

qns_content.text: Which of the following phases is the longest in the cell cycle?

text_solutions: G1 phase is the longest phase of the cell cycle, where cells grow and prepare for DNA replication.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is NOT a function of mitosis?

text_solutions: Gamete formation occurs through meiosis, not mitosis. Mitosis is responsible for growth, repair, and asexual reproduction.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is incorrect about prophase of mitosis?

text_solutions: During prophase, chromosomes condense, the nuclear membrane breaks down, and spindle fibers form, but chromosome alignment occurs in metaphase.

qns_content.text: Which phase of the cell cycle is the longest in a typical eukaryotic cell?

text_solutions: Interphase occupies more than 95% of the cell cycle and includes G1, S, and G2 phases.

qns_content.text: What is the significance of meiosis in sexually reproducing organisms?

options.text: It reduces the chromosome number to half, ensuring genetic diversity
It produces identical cells for growth and repair

text_solutions: Meiosis reduces the chromosome number by half and ensures genetic variation in sexually reproducing organisms.

qns_content.text: Which of the following events occurs during prophase I of meiosis but not in prophase of mitosis?

text_solutions: Crossing over occurs during prophase I of meiosis, leading to genetic recombination, whereas it does not occur in mitosis.

qns_content.text: Which of the following best describes the metaphase plate?

text_solutions: During metaphase, chromosomes align at the metaphase plate, an imaginary plane equidistant from the spindle poles.

qns_content.text: What happens during the diplotene stage of prophase I?

text_solutions: During diplotene, homologous chromosomes start separating as the synaptonemal complex dissolves, but remain attached at chiasmata.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is true about anaphase I of meiosis?

text_solutions: In anaphase I, homologous chromosomes (not sister chromatids) separate and move to opposite poles.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the cell cycle is incorrect?

options.text: Interphase is the longest phase of the cell cycle
G1 phase occurs after the S phase
S phase is responsible for DNA replication

text_solutions: G1 phase occurs before the S phase, not after it.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about interphase is incorrect?

options.text: Interphase consists of G1, S, and G2 phases
Interphase is the shortest phase of the cell cycle
DNA replication occurs in the S phase of interphase

text_solutions: Interphase is the longest phase of the cell cycle, not the shortest.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is incorrect about the G1 phase?

options.text: The cell grows in size during G1 phase
Cells prepare for DNA synthesis in G1 phase

text_solutions: DNA replication does not occur in G1 phase; it happens in the S phase.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is correct about the M checkpoint?

options.text: It ensures that DNA replication is complete
It occurs at the end of G1 phase
It ensures that all chromosomes are attached to spindle fibers before anaphase

text_solutions: The M checkpoint ensures that all chromosomes are properly attached to spindle fibers before anaphase begins.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is correct about anaphase?

options.text: Sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles

text_solutions: During anaphase, sister chromatids separate and are pulled toward opposite poles by spindle fibers.

qns_content.text: Which phase of mitosis immediately follows metaphase?

text_solutions: Anaphase follows metaphase, where sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about telophase is incorrect?

text_solutions: During telophase, sister chromatids have already separated in anaphase; they do not remain attached.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is true about the S phase of interphase?

options.text: DNA replication occurs, doubling the chromosome number
The cell grows and prepares for mitosis

text_solutions: During the S phase, DNA is replicated, doubling the chromosome content of the cell but not the chromosome number.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is an example of a cell type that remains in the G0 phase permanently?

text_solutions: Nerve cells enter G0 phase permanently and do not divide after differentiation.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about the quiescent (G0) phase is correct?

options.text: Cells in G0 phase are metabolically inactive
Nerve and heart cells enter G0 permanently
Cells in G0 phase cannot re-enter the cell cycle
G0 phase occurs after mitosis and before cytokinesis

text_solutions: Nerve and heart cells remain in G0 permanently, while some other cells may re-enter the cycle under specific conditions.

qns_content.text: Which of the following structures plays a crucial role in cytokinesis of plant cells?

text_solutions: In plant cells, cytokinesis occurs via the formation of a cell plate, which eventually develops into a new cell wall.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is incorrect about the centromere?

options.text: It is the region where sister chromatids are attached
Spindle fibers attach to the centromere during cell division
It helps in the separation of homologous chromosomes in meiosis

text_solutions: The centromere remains intact during metaphase and serves as the attachment site for spindle fibers.

qns_content.text: Which of the following occurs at the end of meiosis?

text_solutions: Meiosis results in the formation of four genetically distinct haploid cells.

qns_content.text: During which phase of mitosis does chromatin condense into visible chromosomes?

text_solutions: During prophase, chromatin condenses into distinct chromosomes, making them visible under a microscope.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about meiosis is incorrect?

options.text: Meiosis is a type of asexual reproduction

text_solutions: Meiosis is a type of sexual reproduction, not asexual reproduction.

qns_content.text: What is the role of kinetochores during cell division?

options.text: Act as sites of spindle fiber attachment

text_solutions: Kinetochores are protein structures on the centromere where spindle fibers attach to move chromosomes.

qns_content.text: What is the primary purpose of meiosis II?

text_solutions: Meiosis II is similar to mitosis and is responsible for the separation of sister chromatids into different cells.

qns_content.text: How does meiosis contribute to genetic variation?

options.text: By ensuring identical copies of DNA are passed to daughter cells

text_solutions: Meiosis introduces genetic variation through crossing over during prophase I and independent assortment during metaphase I.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic feature of telophase in mitosis?

text_solutions: Centromeres divide in anaphase, not telophase. In telophase, chromosomes decondense and the nuclear membrane reforms.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is incorrect about metaphase I of meiosis?

options.text: Homologous chromosomes align at the metaphase plate

text_solutions: In metaphase I, homologous chromosomes align at the metaphase plate, but sister chromatids remain together.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about chromatin and chromosomes is correct?

options.text: Chromatin is the condensed form of chromosomes
Chromatin is composed of DNA and proteins

text_solutions: Chromatin consists of DNA and proteins (mainly histones) and condenses into chromosomes during cell division.

qns_content.text: At which stage of mitosis do chromosomes align at the center of the cell?

text_solutions: During metaphase, chromosomes align at the metaphase plate, preparing for equal distribution to daughter cells.

qns_content.text: Which phase of meiosis is responsible for the formation of chiasmata?

text_solutions: During diplotene, homologous chromosomes begin to separate except at chiasmata, where crossing over has occurred.

qns_content.text: What is the function of recombinase enzyme in meiosis?

text_solutions: Recombinase is an enzyme that facilitates crossing over during the pachytene stage of prophase I in meiosis.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about cell division checkpoints is correct?

options.text: G1 checkpoint ensures DNA has replicated correctly
M checkpoint ensures chromosomes are aligned properly

text_solutions: The M checkpoint ensures that all chromosomes are properly aligned before proceeding to anaphase.

qns_content.text: Which structure disappears during prophase of mitosis?

text_solutions: During prophase, the nuclear envelope disintegrates, allowing spindle fibers to attach to chromosomes.

qns_content.text: What is the end result of meiosis in terms of chromosome number?

text_solutions: Meiosis results in haploid cells, ensuring that gametes have half the chromosome number of the parent cell.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is incorrect about prophase I of meiosis?

options.text: It is longer and more complex than prophase of mitosis

text_solutions: Crossing over occurs in the pachytene stage, not in zygotene.

qns_content.text: What is a key difference between meiosis I and meiosis II?

options.text: DNA replication occurs in meiosis I but not in meiosis II
Homologous chromosomes separate in meiosis II, not in meiosis I
Meiosis I produces haploid cells, while meiosis II produces diploid cells

text_solutions: DNA replication occurs only in meiosis I during the S phase, not in meiosis II, which is similar to mitosis.

qns_content.text: Which event is unique to meiosis and does not occur in mitosis?

text_solutions: Crossing over occurs during prophase I of meiosis and is responsible for genetic recombination.

qns_content.text: What is the primary function of the centromere during cell division?

text_solutions: The centromere serves as the attachment site for spindle fibers, ensuring proper chromosome movement during division.

qns_content.text: Which type of cell division occurs in the apical and lateral meristem of plants?

text_solutions: Mitosis occurs in the apical and lateral meristem, leading to the continuous growth of plants.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about meiosis is correct?

options.text: Meiosis occurs in both diploid and haploid cells
Meiosis involves two rounds of cell division
Meiosis results in the production of diploid cells
Meiosis does not contribute to genetic variation

text_solutions: Meiosis consists of two divisions (meiosis I and II) and produces haploid cells, contributing to genetic variation.

qns_content.text: Which event marks the transition from prophase to metaphase in mitosis?

text_solutions: The complete disintegration of the nuclear envelope marks the transition from prophase to metaphase in mitosis.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about prophase is incorrect?

text_solutions: During prophase, the nuclear envelope breaks down, allowing the spindle fibers to interact with chromosomes.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is correct about G2 phase?

options.text: G2 phase occurs before the S phase
The cell checks for DNA replication errors in G2 phase
G2 phase is longer than G1 phase
DNA replication takes place in G2 phase

text_solutions: The G2 phase is a checkpoint where the cell ensures that DNA replication was completed correctly before mitosis begins.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about metaphase is incorrect?

options.text: Metaphase is the best stage to study chromosome morphology

text_solutions: During metaphase, chromosomes align at the metaphase plate, but sister chromatids move to opposite poles in anaphase.

qns_content.text: During which phase of mitosis do spindle fibers attach to kinetochores?

text_solutions: During metaphase, spindle fibers attach to kinetochores and align the chromosomes at the equatorial plate.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is incorrect about genetic variation in meiosis?

text_solutions: Meiosis produces genetically varied cells due to crossing over and independent assortment, not identical ones.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is incorrect about meiosis?

options.text: Meiosis reduces the chromosome number by half
Meiosis consists of one round of division

text_solutions: Meiosis consists of two rounds of division (meiosis I and meiosis II), not just one.

qns_content.text: Which of the following occurs during anaphase II of meiosis?

text_solutions: In anaphase II, sister chromatids separate, similar to anaphase of mitosis.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about mitosis is incorrect?

options.text: Mitosis results in two genetically identical daughter cells
Mitosis is essential for growth and repair

text_solutions: Crossing over does not occur in mitosis; it occurs during prophase I of meiosis.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is incorrect about G2 phase?

text_solutions: DNA replication occurs in the S phase, not in G2.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is incorrect about metaphase?

options.text: Metaphase is an important stage for karyotyping

text_solutions: Sister chromatids do not separate in metaphase; they separate during anaphase.

qns_content.text: Which event distinguishes meiosis I from mitosis?

text_solutions: During meiosis I, homologous chromosomes pair up and undergo recombination, which does not occur in mitosis.

qns_content.text: Which phase of meiosis involves the separation of sister chromatids?

text_solutions: During anaphase II, the sister chromatids of each chromosome separate and move toward opposite poles.

qns_content.text: What is the main feature of metaphase I of meiosis?

options.text: Chromosomes align at the equator as bivalents
Chromatids separate and move to opposite poles

text_solutions: In metaphase I, bivalents (paired homologous chromosomes) align at the metaphase plate.

qns_content.text: What is the function of spindle fibers during cell division?

text_solutions: Spindle fibers attach to kinetochores and help in the movement and separation of chromatids or homologous chromosomes during cell division.

qns_content.text: What happens to the chromosome number during meiosis I?

text_solutions: During meiosis I, homologous chromosomes separate, reducing the chromosome number from diploid to haploid.

qns_content.text: Which of the following occurs during anaphase I but not in mitotic anaphase?

text_solutions: During anaphase I, homologous chromosomes separate, whereas in mitotic anaphase, sister chromatids separate.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about prophase is correct?

text_solutions: During prophase, centrosomes migrate to opposite poles to form the mitotic spindle.

qns_content.text: Which event occurs in anaphase II but not in anaphase I?

text_solutions: In anaphase II, sister chromatids separate, whereas in anaphase I, homologous chromosomes separate.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is incorrect about crossing over in meiosis?

options.text: Crossing over occurs during pachytene of prophase I
It involves exchange of genetic material between homologous chromosomes

text_solutions: Crossing over occurs during pachytene of prophase I, not in metaphase II.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about telophase I of meiosis is incorrect?

text_solutions: There is no DNA replication between meiosis I and II.

qns_content.text: What is the key difference between mitosis and meiosis?

options.text: Mitosis produces haploid cells, meiosis produces diploid cells
Mitosis occurs in gametes, meiosis occurs in somatic cells
Mitosis produces identical cells, meiosis results in genetic variation
Mitosis involves two cell divisions, meiosis involves one

text_solutions: Mitosis produces genetically identical cells, while meiosis introduces genetic variation through recombination.

qns_content.text: Which stage of mitosis is best for studying chromosome morphology?

text_solutions: In metaphase, chromosomes are fully condensed and aligned at the equatorial plate, making them ideal for studying morphology.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is incorrect about the G0 phase?

options.text: G0 is a resting phase where cells do not divide
Nerve and muscle cells remain in G0 permanently
All cells in G0 phase can never re-enter the cell cycle
G0 phase occurs after the G1 phase

text_solutions: Some cells in G0 can re-enter the cell cycle under specific conditions.

qns_content.text: Which of the following events occurs during zygotene of prophase I?

text_solutions: During zygotene, homologous chromosomes pair up in a process called synapsis.

qns_content.text: Which of the following events occurs during telophase II of meiosis?

text_solutions: During telophase II, the nuclear membrane reforms around the newly separated chromosomes.

qns_content.text: Which of the following occurs during zygotene of prophase I?

text_solutions: During zygotene, homologous chromosomes start pairing, a process called synapsis, forming bivalents.

qns_content.text: What is the key difference between cytokinesis in plant and animal cells?

options.text: Plant cells divide by furrowing, while animal cells form a cell plate
Animal cells divide by furrowing, while plant cells form a cell plate
Both plant and animal cells use the same mechanism
Animal cells use microtubules, while plant cells do not

text_solutions: Animal cells divide through cleavage furrow formation, while plant cells form a cell plate during cytokinesis.

qns_content.text: How does mitosis differ from meiosis?

options.text: Mitosis produces four cells, while meiosis produces two
Mitosis results in haploid cells, while meiosis results in diploid cells
Mitosis maintains chromosome number, while meiosis reduces it
Mitosis involves two rounds of division, while meiosis has one

text_solutions: Mitosis maintains the chromosome number, while meiosis reduces it by half, ensuring haploid gamete formation.

qns_content.text: Which checkpoint ensures that DNA replication is complete before mitosis begins?

text_solutions: The G2 checkpoint ensures that DNA replication is complete and checks for errors before the cell enters mitosis.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is incorrect about meiosis I?

options.text: It reduces the chromosome number by half
It includes prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase

text_solutions: Meiosis I produces haploid daughter cells, not diploid.

qns_content.text: Which of the following occurs during the S phase of interphase?

text_solutions: DNA replication occurs in the S phase, ensuring each daughter cell receives an identical set of genetic material.

qns_content.text: What happens during cytokinesis in an animal cell?

text_solutions: In animal cells, cytokinesis occurs by the formation of a cleavage furrow, which deepens to divide the cell into two.

qns_content.text: Which of the following occurs during anaphase I but not in anaphase of mitosis?

text_solutions: During anaphase I, homologous chromosomes separate, while in mitotic anaphase, sister chromatids separate.

qns_content.text: What marks the transition from metaphase to anaphase in mitosis?

text_solutions: During the transition from metaphase to anaphase, sister chromatids separate and begin moving to opposite poles.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is correct about interkinesis?

options.text: Interkinesis is a resting phase between meiosis I and II

text_solutions: Interkinesis is a short resting phase between meiosis I and II, but no DNA replication occurs.

qns_content.text: What is the significance of mitosis?

text_solutions: Mitosis is essential for growth, tissue repair, and asexual reproduction by producing identical cells.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is incorrect about telophase I of meiosis?

text_solutions: There is no DNA replication between meiosis I and II.

qns_content.text: Which stage of meiosis involves crossing over?

text_solutions: During Prophase I, homologous chromosomes undergo crossing over, increasing genetic diversity.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about telophase II is incorrect?

options.text: Nuclear membrane reforms around each set of chromosomes

text_solutions: During telophase II, chromosomes decondense, and nuclear membranes reform.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about metaphase I is incorrect?

options.text: Homologous chromosomes align at the metaphase plate

text_solutions: In metaphase I, homologous chromosomes separate, but sister chromatids remain together.

qns_content.text: Which of the following does NOT occur in interphase?

text_solutions: Chromosome segregation occurs during mitosis, whereas interphase is mainly for growth, DNA replication, and preparation for division.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about G2 phase is correct?

options.text: Cell growth and protein synthesis occur in G2 phase
DNA replication takes place in G2 phase
G2 phase is shorter than M phase

text_solutions: During G2 phase, the cell prepares for mitosis by growing and synthesizing proteins required for division.

qns_content.text: Which phase of the cell cycle is known as the "synthesis phase"?

text_solutions: The S phase (synthesis phase) is when DNA replication occurs, doubling the genetic material in preparation for cell division.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is incorrect about telophase II?

text_solutions: Telophase II results in four haploid cells, not diploid cells.

qns_content.text: What is the key feature of diplotene in meiosis I?

options.text: Separation of homologous chromosomes except at chiasmata

text_solutions: In diplotene, homologous chromosomes start separating but remain attached at chiasmata where crossing over occurred.

qns_content.text: During which phase of meiosis does synapsis occur?

text_solutions: Synapsis occurs during zygotene, where homologous chromosomes pair up and form synaptonemal complexes.

qns_content.text: Which phase in the cell cycle follows DNA replication?

text_solutions: G2 phase follows the S phase and involves the synthesis of proteins required for mitosis.

qns_content.text: Which stage of meiosis ensures the reduction of chromosome number?

text_solutions: In anaphase I, homologous chromosomes separate, reducing the chromosome number by half.

qns_content.text: Which of the following correctly describes cytokinesis in animal cells?

text_solutions: In animal cells, cytokinesis occurs through the formation of a cleavage furrow that pinches the cell into two daughter cells.

qns_content.text: What is the significance of the centromere in mitosis?

options.text: It is the site where spindle fibers attach to chromosomes
It controls the progression of the cell cycle

text_solutions: The centromere is the region where spindle fibers attach during cell division to facilitate chromosome movement.

qns_content.text: Which of the following occurs only in meiosis and not in mitosis?

text_solutions: Homologous chromosome pairing occurs only in meiosis during prophase I, leading to genetic recombination.

qns_content.text: What happens during interkinesis?

text_solutions: Interkinesis is the resting phase between meiosis I and meiosis II, during which no DNA replication occurs.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about genetic variation in meiosis is incorrect?

text_solutions: Meiosis produces genetically varied cells due to crossing over and independent assortment, not identical ones.

qns_content.text: What is the main event during anaphase of mitosis?

options.text: Sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles

text_solutions: During anaphase, the centromeres split, and sister chromatids are pulled to opposite poles by spindle fibers.

qns_content.text: Which of the following statements about meiosis I and meiosis II is incorrect?

options.text: Meiosis I reduces the chromosome number by half
DNA replication occurs before both meiosis I and II

text_solutions: DNA replication occurs only before meiosis I, not between meiosis I and II.

qns_content.text: Which checkpoint ensures that all chromosomes are properly attached to spindle fibers before progressing?

text_solutions: The M checkpoint ensures that all chromosomes are correctly attached to spindle fibers before progressing to anaphase.

qns_content.text:
D, E, F and G are the four daughter cells resulting when cell A undergoes

qns_content.text: One difference between mitosis and meiosis I is that:

options.text: Chromosome do not replicate in the interphase preceding meiosis
Homologous chromosomes pairs synapse during meiosis but not mitosis
Spindle composed of microtubules are not required during meiosis

qns_content.text: What will be the number of the kinetochore in 2 bivalents?
Centrosomes are:

options.text: The central part of the same cell

qns_content.text:
